newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Palestinian on hunger strike in Cyprus detention.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian on hunger strike in Cyprus detention.

text.p: A Palestinian jailed in Cyprus for a deadly bomb attack against the Israeli embassy nine years ago has started a hunger strike, police said on Wednesday.

Omar Hawillo, 31, was sentenced to 15 years in jail for his part in the attack which killed three people in 1988. He was freed and deported to Lebanon in August 1996, but was sent back to Cyprus because Lebanese authorities discovered his passport was forged. He has been held in detention since, unable to find a country willing to accept him.

"I am not a murderer. Whatever I did I did because I believed I was doing something for my country. But does that mean I have to stay until I die in prison without anyone offering me any help?" he told the semi-official Cyprus News Agency from his detention cell on Wednesday.
Hawillo pleaded guilty to two manslaughter charges during his trial. It was never clarified to which Palestinian faction he belonged.

He was arrested after a jeep rigged with explosives went off on a busy Nicosia bridge after security personnel twice prevented the driver from parking outside the Israeli embassy building. The driver of the jeep and two other people were killed.

Cyprus police sources said Hawillo started his hunger strike -- the second this year -- at midday Tuesday on news the authorities had released a group of Iraqis who had remained in detention five months after their prison term expired.

The Iraqis, who do not have travel documents and do not want to return to Iraq, were initially jailed for entering Cyprus illegally. They have been given a three-month resident and employment permit until they find a country willing to accept them.
The Ombudsman's office, which deals with complaints by the public against the civil service, said in a report last week that Hawillo's prolonged detention was "beyond acceptable limits".
